newsitem.title: UK: Refuge adds new security to United offer.
newsitem.headline: Refuge adds new security to United offer.

text.p: Refuge Group Plc said on Monday it would add a new security to be issued to Refuge shareholders in a ratio of three new securities for every one Refuge share held.
In a statement, the company said the new securities would entitle shareholders to receive any extra value in the ordinary branch fund of Refuge Assurance which might be established in the future.
Refuge said its board, however, "continues to believe that no such additional value can, in present circumstances, be released from the ordinary branch fund to Refuge shareholders".

The new security will be in the form of convertible deferred shares of one penny each and any additional value will be represented by conversion of the security into new ordinary shares of the merged businesses of Refuge and United Friendly.

"I am confident that the issue of the new security satisfies the concerns raised by our major shareholders and I look forward to completion of the merger," said John Cudworth, chief executive of Refuge, in a statement.
Refuge said other terms of the merger had not been changed.

The company had said it would consider issuing a new security to give shareholders access to any future surplus assets from its ordinary branch after some major shareholders were wavering on whether to back the deal.
Refuge had delayed its shareholders meeting to approve the merger until October 16.
